directAnswer: SSD performance can drop due to factors like insufficient free space, excessive write cycles, or thermal throttling.
summary: Understanding the causes of SSD performance degradation can help in maintaining optimal speed and longevity.

sections.heading: Insufficient Free Space
sections.body: SSDs require a certain amount of free space for efficient operation. When the drive is nearly full, the performance can degrade significantly due to the lack of room for data management tasks.

sections.heading: Excessive Write Cycles
sections.body: SSDs have a limited number of write cycles. Frequent writing and deleting can wear out the cells, leading to slower performance over time.

sections.heading: Thermal Throttling
sections.body: High temperatures can cause SSDs to throttle their performance to prevent overheating. Ensuring proper cooling can help maintain optimal speeds.

steps.title: Check Free Space
steps.detail: On Windows, open 'This PC' to view available space on your SSD. Aim to keep at least 10-20% free.

steps.title: Monitor Write Cycles
steps.detail: Use tools like CrystalDiskInfo or manufacturer-specific software to monitor the health and write cycles of your SSD.

steps.title: Improve Cooling
steps.detail: Ensure your SSD has adequate airflow. Consider adding case fans or using heat sinks if overheating is an issue.

faqs.question: How much free space should I keep on my SSD?
faqs.answer: It's recommended to keep at least 10-20% of your SSD's capacity free for optimal performance.

faqs.question: Can I recover performance after it drops?
faqs.answer: Yes, freeing up space and reducing write operations can help restore performance to some extent.

faqs.question: Does defragmenting an SSD help with performance?
faqs.answer: No, defragmenting is not necessary for SSDs and can actually reduce their lifespan.

caveats: Performance may vary based on the SSD model and its firmware.
